properties.name: adopt gains a nesting step in Phase 1
properties.rationale:
⭐ THE CHANGE IS ONE BULLET AND THE EVIDENCE FOR IT TOOK A DAY. The flatness had already been measured across seven designs and read TWICE as a fact about users — first as "real designs are two rungs deep so nobody needs depth", then as "the sample is contaminated so nothing can be concluded". Both readings were wrong in the same direction: they treated an instruction's absence as evidence about the world. Anthony's framing is what turned it — *"the hierarchy is there"* — and a trial run on reflow2 itself produced the counterfactual in one pass.

🛑 WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no code changed. `contain_component`, `level` and `hierarchy_issues` all already existed and all already worked; the only thing missing was an instruction to use them. A defect whose fix is a paragraph is worth naming as such, because the temptation on finding a gap this size is to build something.

⚠️ AND THE STEP DOES NOT MAKE DEPTH A TARGET. It says recover what is there and say so when there is nothing. `dec:idea-breadth-and-depth-are-measured-and-the-balance-is-asked-about` records Anthony's own counter-argument — prefer-composition-over-inheritance, deep hierarchies are rigid — and it stands. Today's trial shows depth is RECOVERABLE and that the recovered shape passes span of control; it does not show depth is better, and those are different claims.

📌 THE SYMMETRY IS STILL BROKEN AT THE OTHER END. adopt now recovers the structure an artifact HAS. genesis correctly DEFERS the structure a design NEEDS and nothing derives it — `propose_allocation` exists, is served, and appears in no skill. `dec:idea-does-the-deferred-structuring-step-need-a-skill-of-its-own` holds that question with five options and no answer.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Phase 1 of the adopt skill gains a step it never had: RECOVER THE HIERARCHY THE ARTIFACT HAS. Nest with `contain_component`, set `level` naming a rung on the design's ladder, take the nesting the artifact already shows rather than inventing one.

The bullet carries its own evidence: every design adopt had ever produced came out FLAT — dev_storyflow 101 components with zero containing another, mapwright 15 with zero, music_graph 25 with two — because the instructions never once said to nest. Re-run on reflow2 itself with only this step added, the same artifact yielded four rungs, `hierarchy_issues` 0, and no parent over the 3–7 span-of-control bound, while the hand-built functional design of the same system exceeds it in four places.

It also states two limits so the step is not mistaken for the whole job: FLAT IS AN HONEST ANSWER when the artifact is flat, and nesting cannot recover the FUNCTIONAL carving — measured twice on reflow2 (86 core modules loose in one directory; a star-shaped import graph with three hubs at fan-in 49/42/41 and 45% of modules importing only those). That half comes from purpose, with the user, and belongs to genesis.

`skill_lint` caught three things and named the fix for each: `level` is a node PROPERTY not a served tool (added to NON_TOOL_TERMS with its reason), and the `.claude/skills` and `.grok/skills` mirrors were stale (re-copied). Skills are compiled into the binary by build.rs, so `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` is what makes the change actually serve.
